raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

The PD mini load balancer's `/health` returns 200 without contacting any server. A health check on the LB therefore stays green while every prefill and decode engine is down. `/health_generate` is also blind. It returns 200 when an engine answers 503, and a bare 500 when an engine refuses the connection.

This first appeared in sglang-torchtpu (sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu#1274) and was fixed there in sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu#1576. The code is the same here. The TPU P/D recipes install `sglang-router` from PyPI, so they only get the fix once it lands in this repo.

## Modifications

- `/health` and `/health_generate` now probe every registered prefill and decode server in parallel.
  - They return 200 only if every server answers 200.
  - Otherwise they return 503 with `{"unhealthy": [{role, url, status, error}]}`.
  - A role with no registered server also returns 503. A runtime role switch can cause this briefly.
  - Probes time out after 30 s. That is above the engine's own `SGLANG_HEALTH_CHECK_TIMEOUT` (20 s by default), after which the engine answers 503 itself.
- The check is strict on purpose. MiniLB picks a backend at random and does not track health, so one dead server already fails part of the traffic. The Rust gateway's `/readiness` (any healthy prefill AND any healthy decode) fits the Rust gateway, because it skips unhealthy workers.
- New `/liveness` endpoint. It returns 200 while the LB process is up, which is the old `/health` behavior.

**Callers in this repo.** The disaggregation test fixtures (`disaggregation_fixture.py`, the Ascend/NPU PD tests, `test_mori_transfer_engine_e2e.py`, `test_tracing_disaggregation.py`) wait for every engine's `/health` before they poll the LB's `/health`. The stricter check only adds probe latency for them.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable. No model, kernel or forward-path change.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. Each health call adds one concurrent probe per backend.

## Validation

- New `tests/test_mini_lb_health.py`. It serves real aiohttp backends that answer 200 or 503/500, refuse connections, or hang. It also covers a role with no registered server, `/liveness`, and route registration.
- `pytest tests` with `--cov-fail-under=80`: the coverage gate passes at 87.75%. `mini_lb.py` is omitted from coverage by `.coveragerc`.
  - I used this tree's Python sources with the Rust extension from the PyPI 0.3.2 wheel. That mismatch fails 13 `test_pyo3_binding.py` cases, both with and without this change.
  - In sglang-torchtpu CI, where the wheel is built from source, the same suite gave 128 passed.
- End to end through `python -m sglang_router.launch_router --pd-disaggregation --mini-lb`, with stand-in prefill and decode servers in separate processes:

| Scenario | Endpoint | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| all up | `/health`, `/health_generate`, `/generate` | 200 | 200 |
| decode answers 503 | `/health` / `/health_generate` | 200 / 200 | 503 / 503, decode listed |
| decode killed | `/health` / `/health_generate` | 200 / 500 | 503 / 503, decode listed |
| both killed | `/health` / `/health_generate` | 200 / 500 | 503 / 503, both listed |
| any | `/liveness` | 404 | 200 |

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (No mini-LB health docs exist.)
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (Not applicable.)
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

The only failing checks are `pr-gate`, because the PR has no `run-ci` label, and this account can't add it. Could you comment `/tag-and-rerun-ci` to start CI? Thanks!

Hi @CatherineSue @key4ng @slin1237, could one of you take a look at #45747 (mini-LB `/health` and `/health_generate` return 503 while a backend is down)? It has an approval from @hlFu, but merging also needs a review from a `sgl-model-gateway/bindings/python` code owner. All required checks pass. The red ones aren't from this change: `chat-completions-4gpu` fails on an NCCL error at worker startup on the GPU runner (it also fails on main in 3 of its last 5 runs), and the `PR Test Extra` gates are opt-in. Once approved, could someone with write access merge it? Thanks!

@sherlockwu thanks! Yes. With this change, `/health` and `/health_generate` return 200 only when every registered prefill and decode server answers 200. MiniLB routes randomly with no health tracking, so one dead server already fails part of the traffic. The 503 body lists the unhealthy servers, and `/liveness` keeps the old process-only check. This is spelled out in the `_probe_backends` docstring.

One CI question: `chat-completions-4gpu` failed on a flaky NCCL error at worker startup, and `/rerun-failed-ci` can't retry it. The re-run stops at "Download wheel artifact" (`Artifact not found for name: smg-wheel`) because the original wheel artifact has expired. A new push would dismiss the approvals, so could you use "Re-run all jobs" on the PR Test (SMG) run (https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39819446502)? That rebuilds the wheel and retries the job. All required checks are already green.
The sglang-torchtpu side of this fix is merged: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/pull/1576 (fixes sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu#1274).

thanks, lgtm. 
And note health check pass == every backend is healthy in this case.

 )  # 64KB, to prevent aiohttp's "Chunk too big" error
 
+# A server's /health and /health_generate run a one-token generation by default
+# and give up after SGLANG_HEALTH_CHECK_TIMEOUT (20 s by default) with a 503;
+# wait a little longer so the server's own answer arrives.
+HEALTH_CHECK_TIMEOUT_SECS = 30
+
 
 def maybe_wrap_ipv6_address(address: str) -> str:
     try:
@@ -274,21 +279,64 @@ async def stream_results():
 lb: Optional[MiniLoadBalancer] = None
 
 
+async def _probe_backends(path: str) -> Response:
+    """GET `path` on every registered server; 200 only if all answer 200.
+
+    MiniLB routes to every registered server and does not track their health,
+    so a single dead server already fails part of the traffic. This is stricter
+    than the Rust gateway's /readiness, which skips unhealthy workers.
+    """
+    timeout = HEALTH_CHECK_TIMEOUT_SECS
+
+    async def probe(session, server):
+        try:
+            async with session.get(f"{server}{path}") as response:
+                return response.status, None
+        except asyncio.TimeoutError:
+            return None, f"no answer in {timeout} s"
+        except aiohttp.ClientError as e:
+            return None, f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"
+
+    roles = {"prefill": list(lb.prefill_urls), "decode": list(lb.decode_urls)}
+    backends = [(role, url) for role, urls in roles.items() for url in urls]
+    async with aiohttp.ClientSession(
+        timeout=aiohttp.ClientTimeout(total=timeout)
+    ) as session:
+        results = await asyncio.gather(*(probe(session, url) for _, url in backends))
+    unhealthy = [
+        {"role": role, "url": url, "status": status, "error": error}
+        for (role, url), (status, error) in zip(backends, results)
+        if status != 200
+    ]
+    # A role switch can briefly leave a role with no registered server.
+    unhealthy += [
+        {"role": role, "url": None, "status": None, "error": "no server registered"}
+        for role, urls in roles.items()
+        if not urls
+    ]
+    if not unhealthy:
+        return Response(status_code=200)
+    logger.warning(f"[MiniLB] {path}: unhealthy backends {unhealthy}")
+    return ORJSONResponse(
+        content={"unhealthy": unhealthy},
+        status_code=HTTPStatus.SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE,
+    )
+
+
+@app.get("/liveness")
+async def liveness():
+    """200 while the MiniLB process serves requests; ignores the backends."""
+    return Response(status_code=200)
+
+

+"""MiniLB /health and /health_generate must report the backends, not only the
+LB process: MiniLB routes to every registered server without health tracking,
+so one dead server already fails part of the traffic."""
+
+import asyncio
+import json
+import socket
+
+import pytest
+from aiohttp import web
+from sglang_router import mini_lb
+
+# Backend behaviors: an HTTP status, refused connection, or no answer at all.
+REFUSED = "refused"
+HANGS = "hangs"
+
+
+def _handler(behavior, release):
+    async def handler(request):
+        if behavior == HANGS:
+            # Released at teardown; the runner's cleanup waits for handlers.
+            await release.wait()
+            return web.Response(status=503)
+        return web.Response(status=behavior)
+
+    return handler
+
+
+async def _serve(behavior, release):
+    app = web.Application()
+    app.router.add_get("/health", _handler(behavior, release))
+    app.router.add_get("/health_generate", _handler(behavior, release))
+    runner = web.AppRunner(app)
+    await runner.setup()
+    site = web.TCPSite(runner, "127.0.0.1", 0)
+    await site.start()
+    port = site._server.sockets[0].getsockname()[1]
+    return runner, f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}"
+
+
+def _refused_url():
+    """URL of a local port that nothing listens on."""
+    with socket.socket() as sock:
+        sock.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
+        port = sock.getsockname()[1]
+    return f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}"
+
+
+def _run(monkeypatch, handler, prefill_behaviors, decode_behaviors):
+    """Serve one backend per behavior, point MiniLB at them, and call
+    `handler`. Returns the response and the prefill and decode URLs."""
+
+    async def run():
+        runners = []
+        release = asyncio.Event()
+
+        async def backend_url(behavior):
+            if behavior == REFUSED:
+                return _refused_url()
+            runner, url = await _serve(behavior, release)
+            runners.append(runner)
+            return url
+
+        try:
+            prefill_urls = [await backend_url(b) for b in prefill_behaviors]
+            decode_urls = [await backend_url(b) for b in decode_behaviors]
+            load_balancer = mini_lb.MiniLoadBalancer.__new__(mini_lb.MiniLoadBalancer)
+            load_balancer.timeout = 3600
+            load_balancer.prefill_urls = prefill_urls
+            load_balancer.prefill_bootstrap_ports = [8998] * len(prefill_urls)
+            load_balancer.decode_urls = decode_urls
+            monkeypatch.setattr(mini_lb, "lb", load_balancer)
+            return await handler(), prefill_urls, decode_urls
+        finally:
+            release.set()
+            for runner in runners:
+                await runner.cleanup()
+
+    return asyncio.run(run())
+
+
+@pytest.mark.unit
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("handler", [mini_lb.health_check, mini_lb.health_generate])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("prefill_behaviors", "decode_behaviors", "expected_status", "unhealthy"),
+    [
+        pytest.param([200], [200], 200, [], id="all_healthy"),
+        pytest.param([503], [200], 503, [("prefill", 0, 503)], id="prefill_503"),
+        pytest.param([200], [REFUSED], 503, [("decode", 0, None)], id="decode_down"),
+        pytest.param(
+            [REFUSED],
+            [REFUSED],
+            503,
+            [("prefill", 0, None), ("decode", 0, None)],
+            id="both_down",
+        ),
+        pytest.param(
+            [200], [200, 500], 503, [("decode", 1, 500)], id="one_of_two_decodes"
+        ),
+        pytest.param([HANGS], [200], 503, [("prefill", 0, None)], id="prefill_hangs"),
+        pytest.param(
+            [200], [], 503, [("decode", None, None)], id="no_decode_registered"
+        ),
+    ],
+)
+def test_health_reports_backends(
+    monkeypatch,
+    handler,
+    prefill_behaviors,
+    decode_behaviors,
+    expected_status,
+    unhealthy,
+):
+    monkeypatch.setattr(mini_lb, "HEALTH_CHECK_TIMEOUT_SECS", 1)
+
+    response, prefill_urls, decode_urls = _run(
+        monkeypatch, handler, prefill_behaviors, decode_behaviors
+    )
+
+    assert response.status_code == expected_status
+    if expected_status == 200:
+        return
+    urls = {"prefill": prefill_urls, "decode": decode_urls}
+    reported = json.loads(response.body)["unhealthy"]
+    assert [(b["role"], b["url"], b["status"]) for b in reported] == [
+        (role, None if index is None else urls[role][index], status)
+        for role, index, status in unhealthy
+    ]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.unit
+def test_hung_backend_reports_timeout(monkeypatch):
+    monkeypatch.setattr(mini_lb, "HEALTH_CHECK_TIMEOUT_SECS", 1)
+
+    response, _, _ = _run(monkeypatch, mini_lb.health_check, [200], [HANGS])
+
+    assert response.status_code == 503
+    assert json.loads(response.body)["unhealthy"][0]["error"] == "no answer in 1 s"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.unit
+def test_liveness_ignores_backends(monkeypatch):
+    response, _, _ = _run(monkeypatch, mini_lb.liveness, [REFUSED], [REFUSED])
+    assert response.status_code == 200
+
+
+@pytest.mark.unit
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("path", "endpoint"),
+    [
+        ("/health", mini_lb.health_check),
+        ("/health_generate", mini_lb.health_generate),
+        ("/liveness", mini_lb.liveness),
+    ],
+)
+def test_health_routes_are_registered(path, endpoint):
+    routes = {route.path: route.endpoint for route in mini_lb.app.routes}
+    assert routes[path] is endpoint
